name: dispatch_contention
fields: scheduler.policy.dispatch_interval_cycles (new, constant per device; absent / 1 = the present one-issue-per-cycle SMSP model)
motivation: Round 32 (single-cluster loop): 32-cycle ncu warp-stall sampling on fa3_fwd_hdim_small_05 / fa3_fwd_fp8_03 / fa3_bwd_06 (H100) shows the softmax instruction stream taking ~2x the engine's time while the engine is tensor-pipe bound (97 % vs 77 % hardware pipe utilisation): a dependent FMNMX chain (control-word stall 4 + yield) costs 11 cycles per instruction on hardware against 4.9 in the engine, MUFU.EX2 7.9 k vs 4.1 k kernel cycles, and the hardware stall reasons there are dispatch (15 % of all samples) and not_selected (8 %) with 3 consumer warps per SMSP. The engine's SMSP issue model is one instruction per cycle per SMSP plus the per-class issue_interval on its execution unit (service_latency 'thr' cells, measured with a single warp) plus the control-word stall floor (round 30). Whether a dispatcher-level cost that only appears with several warps per SMSP exists has never been measured.
engine_rule_declared_before_data: Candidate A (class-independent): every issued warp-instruction occupies the SMSP dispatcher for d cycles, so an SMSP issues at most one instruction per d cycles (scheduler.policy.dispatch_interval_cycles = d, fractional accumulation as for resources.json initiation intervals; d <= 1 means the present model). Candidate B (class-specific): the per-class issue_interval_cycles already models the unit; a W-dependent excess that differs by class beyond candidate A is reported per class and NOT installed by this protocol (it would need the class leaf's own protocol). Candidate C: no excess -> nothing installed. The decision rule between A / B / C is fixed below.
probe: tools/microbench/dispatch_contention/probe/contention.cu, one CTA of 4*W warps (W in {1, 2, 3, 4}: warp w sits on SMSP w % 4, so every SMSP holds W warps running the same code), every warp times its own window with clock64 (t_s / t_w), medians over warps x launches x reps. Window = U units of a dependent chain on one register, U in {64, 128, 256}, straight-line (fully unrolled, no loop). Chain variants: ffma `d = fma(d, a, b)`; fmnmx `d = fmaxf(d, c_i)` (c_i from a 4-register ring so no reuse of the same source); mufu `ex2.approx.ftz.f32 d, d` (inline asm); imad `d = d * a + b` (u32); mixed `ffma; fmnmx` alternating on the same register. Plus an independent-stream variant ilp8: each warp runs 8 independent FFMA accumulator chains interleaved (issue-rate bound, not latency bound), U counted per instruction. a, b, c_i come from kernel arguments read before t_s. The same binary runs all W (blockDim = 128 * W). --launches 16 --reps 65, two runs (run-a, run-b) per device.
sass_gate: tools/microbench/dispatch_contention/sass_check.py: between t_s and t_w the kernel contains exactly U instructions of the variant's class (FFMA / FMNMX / MUFU.EX2 / IMAD; mixed: U/2 + U/2; ilp8: U FFMA) and no other instruction except at most one MOV per register ring element before the window; the chain register dependence must be real (each instruction's destination is a source of the next, ilp8 excepted); the control words (stall, yield, scoreboards) of every window instruction are recorded per variant and reported (the installed result latencies are expected to appear as the stall counts). A variant failing the gate on a device is unrealised there.

derivation.T(variant, W, U): median over warps x launches x reps of (t_w - t_s) in cycles (per warp; W >= 2 means every SMSP hosts W such warps simultaneously)
derivation.slope(variant, W): OLS slope of T over U (cycles per chain step)
derivation.P(variant, W): prediction of the present engine model from the device's installed leaves: dependent chains max(L_class, W * ii_class), where L_class = instruction.service result_latency_cycles (the fixed-latency dependency distance; must equal the window's control-word stall count) and ii_class = the class's issue_interval_cycles on its execution unit; mixed (one FFMA then one FMNMX per pair of steps, different units): per instruction max((L_ffma + L_fmnmx) / 2, W * max(ii_ffma, ii_fmnmx) / 2); ilp8 (issue bound): per instruction max(1, W * ii_ffma)
derivation.excess(variant, W): slope - P (cycles per instruction; >= 0 means the hardware is slower than the present model)
derivation.d(variant, W): for W >= 2: slope / W when slope > P, i.e. the per-instruction dispatcher occupancy implied if the excess is dispatcher-side
derivation.decision: C (nothing) if excess(variant, W) <= max(2 % of slope, 1 cycle) for all variants and W. Otherwise compute d over all (variant, W >= 2) cells with positive excess: if their relative spread (max - min) / median <= 10 % and the W = 1 cells show excess <= 1 cycle (a dispatcher cost is invisible with a single warp when L >= d) -> A with dispatch_interval_cycles = median d (measured if both runs agree within 3 %, else experimental); if the d values differ by class beyond 10 % -> B: per-class excess reported in the model output and docs/en/microbench.md, nothing installed. ilp8 is a consistency check for A: its slope must equal max(1, W * max(ii_ffma, d)) within 5 %, otherwise A is downgraded to experimental.

acceptance.cell: OLS residual <= 2 % and run-a / run-b agreement <= 3 % (or <= 1 cycle) -> the cell is usable; cells failing this are excluded from the decision and listed
acceptance.both devices: each device decides and installs on its own data; no cross-device fill
acceptance.negative excess: a slope below P by more than 2 % is reported (it would mean an installed class leaf is too slow), not acted on here

install: A only: common/mechanisms/scheduler.policy.json gains field dispatch_interval_cycles (constant); <arch>/leaves/scheduler.policy.json carries d with source dispatch_contention.<device>.<run>; engine: Simulator's per-SMSP issue admits one instruction per dispatch_interval_cycles (fractional accumulator), default 1 when the field is absent; a CTest fixture (two warps on one SMSP, d = 2 -> alternate issue every 2 cycles; d absent -> every cycle); tree build && tree validate --strict; one two-architecture 500 A/B round against the current baseline.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no change of the decision rule, thresholds or variants after data; the yield bit and the control-word stall counts are facts of the program and are not modelled by this protocol (round 30 already applies the stall floor).

addenda.written_before: run r2 on either device; after reading r1 (h100-r1 / b300-r1) model.json
addenda.text: (probe defect, r1) k_cell has no barrier between repetitions: the 4*W warps start together but drift, so a window of a later repetition is not guaranteed to overlap the other warps' windows. The dependent-chain cells of r1 (ffma / fmnmx / imad / mufu: slopes 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 8 per step for W 1..4 on both devices, integer-like) are consistent with full overlap, but ilp8 with W >= 2 reports 1.00 cycle per instruction per warp, i.e. W warp-instructions per cycle per SMSP, which exceeds the SMSP's 32 FP32 lanes - that cell cannot have overlapped. r2 adds `bar.sync 0` (all 128*W threads) immediately before every repetition's t_s so every window starts with all W warps of each SMSP at the same instruction; probe-only change, variants / derivation / decision rule unchanged; r1 is kept as a record and not used for the decision. Reading of r1 for the record: IMAD and FMNMX follow the present model exactly (max(4, 2W): 16-lane units); FFMA dependent chains follow 2W as well although the installed FFMA issue_interval is ~1 (dual 16-lane pipes, single-warp independent stream 1 / cycle): a dependent FP32 chain appears confined to one 16-lane pipe; mixed ffma/fmnmx carries control-word stall 5 (cross-pipe dependency, already honoured by the stall floor); h100 MUFU.EX2 chain is 17.07 against the installed MUFU result 23 (negative excess, reported).

addenda.written_before: any r3 run; after reading r2 (h100-r2 / b300-r2)
addenda.text: (reading of r2; decision B on both devices, nothing installed) The per-warp window cannot measure issue-bound contention: with stall-1 instructions the SMSP scheduler runs one warp's whole window before switching (greedy / cursor-commit), so every warp's own t_w - t_s stays 257 for 256 FFMAs at any W although the SMSP cannot issue 4 warp-FFMA per cycle; ilp8 is therefore uninformative for candidate A (not a refutation) and an issue-rate cell needs a CTA-wide window (barrier -> last warp's t_w, or globaltimer) in a future version. Dependent chains do interleave (a warp with stall 4 cannot hold the slot) and give: FMNMX / IMAD exactly max(4, 2W) = the present model (16-lane units, ii 2); MUFU.EX2 h100 17.07 per step at W <= 2 (installed MUFU result 23 is too slow for EX2; W = 3 / 4 follow the 8.26 unit interval), b300 14 = installed; FFMA 4 / 5 / 6 / 8 for W = 1..4 on both devices against the present max(4, W x 1.045): a dependent FP32 chain behaves as a 2-cycle (16-lane) unit when several warps' chains interleave, while a single warp's independent stream issues 1 / cycle (service_latency thr, two 16-lane FP32 pipes). Whether cross-warp independent FP32 streams reach 1 / cycle (both pipes usable by any warp) or 0.5 (the second pipe only pairs same-warp consecutive instructions) is not decided by this data; a version 2 with an ilp2 variant and a CTA-wide window is the way to settle the FP32 pipe model before any FFMA / FMUL / FADD leaf change.
